question: Two trains travelling in opposite directions cross each other in 25 seconds. If the length of both the trains is 250 m each and the speed of one of them is 45 km/hr, what would be the speed of the other train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = 250 m + 250 m = 500 m.

Relative speed = Distance ÷ Time = 500 ÷ 25 = 20 m/s.

Convert relative speed to km/hr = 20 × (18 ÷ 5) = 72 km/hr.

Speed of the other train = Relative speed − First train speed = 72 − 45 = 27 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train, L₁ = 250 m

Length of second train, L₂ = 250 m

Speed of first train, S₁ = 45 km/hr

Time taken to cross each other, T = 25 seconds
